version.changelog:
Version 1.0.5 of duhui-all-to-pdf

- No code or file changes detected.
- Audit and behavioral instructions in SKILL.md updated:
  - Adjusted privacy and user notice terms regarding AppCode handling.
  - Removed the explicit required user disclosure before uploading, but core privacy practices remain.
  - Clarified agent behavior when handling DUHUI_ALI_APPCODE.
- No changes to the technical workflow or skill usage.

llm.summary: The skill is a disclosed cloud document-to-PDF converter, but it can upload local documents to third-party storage under broad triggers without a strong consent boundary.

dimensions.detail: Network access, local file read/write, and DUHUI_ALI_APPCODE are coherent for this cloud workflow, but arbitrary user documents may be sensitive, remote cleanup is best-effort, and the returned pdf_url is downloaded without host or content validation.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: No package installer, dependency installation, startup hook, background service, or install-time mutation was found; the artifact consists of SKILL.md, one reference file, and one Python script.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Activation is broad for generic document/PDF conversion, while the workflow immediately uploads the selected local file after only a stderr privacy notice; it does not require an explicit per-run confirmation or consent flag before third-party transfer.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The script does not persist secrets to disk and only caches OSS credentials in process memory, but it may leave source documents temporarily in vendor-controlled OSS if cleanup fails and documents remote result URLs in output.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The main behavior matches the stated purpose: convert one local document to PDF through Duhui/Alibaba APIs, using a Python standard-library script, one AppCode environment variable, vendor endpoints, and local output writing.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if users understand that selected local documents will be uploaded to Duhui/Alibaba-controlled infrastructure in the cn-shanghai OSS flow. Use it for non-sensitive files or after explicit consent, prefer local conversion for confidential documents, provide AppCode through an environment variable or secret store rather than chat, and restrict network access to the documented endpoints where possible.
llm.findings:
[TT3] unexpected: Downgraded: the cited urlopen sink downloads the vendor-returned pdf_url, not DUHUI_ALI_APPCODE; AppCode is sent as an Authorization header to the documented conversion API, which is expected for this service.
[TP2] unexpected: Downgraded: the mixed Chinese and ASCII in the skill name appears descriptive rather than a spoofed tool identifier or tool-poisoning attempt.
[LP3] expected: Accepted as a scoping concern: the required file read/write, environment secret, and outbound network capabilities are disclosed and purpose-aligned, but not constrained by an explicit permission block.
[SQP-1] unexpected: Accepted: broad generic triggers such as document conversion and PDF conversion are overbroad for a workflow that uploads files to third-party infrastructure.
[E1] expected: Accepted in context: external transmission is not covert exfiltration because it is the core documented conversion path, but it remains sensitive because local document contents leave the host and remote cleanup is best-effort.
[SDI-4] unexpected: Accepted in part: the artifact mostly prefers environment or secret-store handling and forbids echoing AppCode, but the chat-consent line is ambiguous and should be tightened.
[SQP-2] unexpected: Accepted: reference and workflow documentation disclose the upload but do not enforce explicit user consent or sensitivity checks before transmission.
[SDI-2] expected: Accepted as disclosed integration behavior: fetching temporary OSS credentials at runtime is documented and only cached in memory, but it adds a vendor-controlled credential bootstrap trust boundary.
[SDI-1] expected: Downgraded: returning pdf_url and source_object_key is documented in the SKILL.md output contract, so it is not hidden behavior.
[T09] unexpected: Accepted in part from static scan: third-party upload is purpose-aligned, but missing enforced consent and unvalidated vendor download URLs are material review concerns.
